Act as a Creative Director, Art Director, Editorial Photographer, and Luxury Campaign Storyteller. Analyse the attached reference image to identify: the subject (person), the world/location, lighting logic, mood, color grammar, and any objects already visible in the frame. Then write exactly 9 distinct image-generation prompts for a cohesive high-end editorial storyboard that tells this person's story across 9 completely distinct frames, shot on the same campaign set.


The storyboard must preserve the exact visual world, location, subject identity, lighting, mood, and colour language of the reference image. The reference image defines world, location, subject, atmosphere, and visual style — but NOT pose, framing, camera angle, action, or composition. Every frame must read as a new photograph from the same shoot, with a distinct photographic approach and focal length per frame.


SUPPORTING PROP LOGIC (no product node exists — this is the default, not a fallback):
Study the reference image's setting, mood, and implied lifestyle to infer 2–4 plausible props that would naturally belong to this person in this world (e.g. a water bottle, a cigarette, a bicycle, sunglasses, a tote bag, a paperback, a coffee cup — chosen from what the scene logically suggests, not copied verbatim from this list). Assign these across 2–4 of the 9 frames only. Never place more than one prop per frame unless they form one coherent action (e.g. sunglasses pushed up while gripping bicycle handlebars). Props must feel incidental and lived-in — small narrative texture, never competing with the person as visual hero. In each prop frame, state explicitly how it's held, worn, or positioned. The remaining 5–7 frames carry no added props — pure subject and environment.


Every prompt MUST end with this exact sentence: "Inherit the visual DNA of the attached reference image as a continuous editorial campaign. The environment, architectural backdrop, location setting, lighting style, color grading, mood, texture language, subject/character identity, wardrobe logic, and objects presence must remain EXACTLY consistent with the reference image."


CHARACTER COVERAGE — across the 9 frames you must include:
- At least 2 frames shot from behind (walking away, looking over shoulder, back/shoulders/posture as subject)
- At least 1 frame shot from above (overhead/bird's-eye)
- At least 2 close-up frames (face, hands, expression or feature detail)
- At least 1 wide environmental frame establishing them in the world
- No two frames share the same pose, angle, or body orientation (standing, seated, mid-motion, leaning, turning, reclining, etc.)
- Distinct emotional/narrative beats per frame (arrival, stillness, motion, contemplation, interaction with environment or prop, departure, etc.)


LENS COVERAGE — use a different focal length/approach in every frame. Across the 9 prompts, include: 14mm ultra-wide, 20mm wide architectural, 24mm low-angle hero, 35mm documentary, 50mm natural eye-level, 85mm portrait, 105mm compressed detail, 135mm telephoto, and macro detail. Never repeat camera distance, lens behaviour, or composition type between any two frames.


PHOTOGRAPHIC QUALITY — render every frame to studio-grade fidelity: crisp focus, refined dynamic range, color grading matched to the reference image, and high-fidelity material textures (skin, fabric, surfaces, metal). Skin must show natural, uniform, true-to-life texture (pores, fine detail) — no plastic smoothing, no patchy transitions, no visible repair seams. Lighting must read as professional studio or location lighting with falloff and shadow depth consistent with the reference image's light source.


NO TEXT RULE — strictly forbid any visible text, typography, signage, captions, labels, logos, symbols, brand marks, watermarks, posters, screens, or written elements anywhere in frame — including on any inferred prop (e.g. a water bottle must be unmarked and label-free). Describe any naturally-branded object as unmarked, clean, and label-free while preserving its form and material identity.


FORMAT — each prompt must be 80–150 words, one continuous paragraph, enclosed in quotation marks, separated by exactly ONE blank line. Write like an elite luxury campaign treatment. No bullets, titles, headings, intros, analysis, explanations, closing notes, or numbering outside the quotes. Output ONLY the 9 quoted, numbered paragraphs. Each prompt must include @[595f9105-9c07-4dcd-b52e-51a00b8743bf] description.
